investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-18T06:57–07:05Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the Pending state, so the eval runner could not reach the agent creation or readiness steps required by the expected-output contract.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 nodes that carry it. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" was reproduced identically (with only minor timing differences of 137 s, 143 s, and 146 s) across all three sibling checks, confirming the resource pool is fully consumed and preemption cannot free any capacity. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure localized to the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource pool in the production-api environment; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact is scoped to the observability eval.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource fully consumed on both eligible nodes: all available VM slots are occupied by existing remote agent pods or other workloads, leaving zero capacity for new pods. Preemption was explicitly ruled out by the scheduler ('No preemption victims found'), meaning no lower-priority pods are evictable.

SECONDARY — Node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy, reducing the schedulable pool to those 2 nodes. If those 2 nodes are also at capacity, any new pod is immediately Unschedulable regardless of cluster-wide free resources.

TERTIARY — Cluster autoscaler not configured or not triggered for kata.peerpods.io/vm nodes: if the node group backing peer-pod VMs does not scale out automatically, resource exhaustion is permanent until existing pods are deleted or nodes are manually added.

QUATERNARY — Eval probe concurrency: all three sibling checks ran within the same ~7-minute window and each attempted to create a separate remote agent pod, potentially competing for the same scarce VM slots and collectively exhausting capacity faster than any single check would.

investigation.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-18T07:00–07:05Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes cannot place new kata peer-pod VMs because 2 nodes report insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the agent pod never schedules, the eval runner's createAgent call never completes, no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) is written, and the expected-output contract for remote-agent-state is fully violated.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource across all eligible nodes. Of the 6 nodes in the cluster, only 2 are eligible for kata peer-pod scheduling (the other 4 do not match the pod's node affinity/selector), and those 2 nodes have no remaining kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity. Preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist on those nodes. As a result, every remote-agent pod submitted during the eval window is stuck in Unschedulable state for ~137–147 seconds before the eval times out, preventing any agent lifecycle progress and leaving all required evidence fields empty.

investigation.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes Kata PeerPods VM Resource Exhaustion Blocking Pod Scheduling
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api on 2026-07-18 with identical Kubernetes scheduler messages indicating that the 6-node cluster has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource capacity on the 2 eligible nodes, and the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity or selector. Because no remote agent pod could be scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call never completed, no evidence was collected, and the expected-output contract for remote-agent-runtime (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) was entirely unmet. This is an eval-infrastructure and underlying Kubernetes cluster resource failure; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature in production-api has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 nodes that match the pod's node affinity/selector. With 0 of 6 nodes available and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote agent pod submitted by the eval runner is stuck Unschedulable. The eval runner at infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs (line 1918) calls createAgent with type "remote", which requires a kata peer-pod VM slot. Because the pod never starts, the agent is never created, no runtime response is produced, and all five required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) remain missing, causing the contract validation to fail completely.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes Kata PeerPods VM Resource Exhaustion Blocking Pod Scheduling
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api on 2026-07-18 with identical Kubernetes scheduler messages indicating that the 6-node cluster has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource capacity on the 2 eligible nodes, and the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity or selector. Because no remote agent pod could be scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call never completed, no evidence was collected, and the expected-output contract for remote-agent-runtime (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) was entirely unmet. This is an eval-infrastructure and underlying Kubernetes cluster resource failure; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature in production-api has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 nodes that match the pod's node affinity/selector. With 0 of 6 nodes available and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote agent pod submitted by the eval runner is stuck Unschedulable. The eval runner at infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs (line 1918) calls createAgent with type "remote", which requires a kata peer-pod VM slot. Because the pod never starts, the agent is never created, no runtime response is produced, and all five required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) remain missing, causing the contract validation to fail completely.
